SEC26A-01.note: Plural 'the young' takes 'are'; 'their' refers to the nestlings whose begging is answered. 'its' tempts via 'the nest'/'the breeding female'.

SEC26A-02.note: 'Each of the patients' is singular; past progressive set by 'when the sponsor put the trial on hold'. 'wards'/'patients' pull toward plural.

SEC26A-03.note: 'kept nearest the freezer's door' is restrictive (it identifies which of many trays), so no comma. B is attractive as a supplementary participle; D splits the participle from its complement.

SEC26A-04.note: Singular 'ointment' plus 'since ... last spring' requires present perfect 'has been prescribed'. 'clinics'/'network' distract.

SEC26A-05.note: Subject 'the needles' is plural; agent pronoun 'them' refers to the acid-tolerant bacteria. Adjacent singular 'pine' pulls toward 'is' and 'it'.

SEC26A-06.note: Plural 'oats', past frame ('credited'), and the predicate adjective 'rotten' needs 'were'; 'has/have seldom ... rotten' lacks a participle.

SEC26A-07.note: Two independent clauses; period. Colon (D) is the strongest distractor but the second clause does not explain the first. B splice, C fused.

SEC26A-08.note: Singular 'pancreas'; present tense governed by 'receive'. Adjacent 'mice' pulls toward plural.

SEC26A-09.note: Cooperative of many growers, so plural possessive 'growers''; contrast with the founder's own trees. 'grower's' tempts via the single founder.

SEC26A-10.note: Intro clause 'Before the workers could spray' ends before 'the vines', which is the subject of 'were showing'. Garden path makes A/B attractive; D leaves a fragment.

SEC26B-01.note: Plural 'engineers' takes 'have'; 'it' = the status report. Long Although-clause with 'report' and 'interference' separates.

SEC26B-02.note: Singular 'front'; present habitual set by 'whenever ... drain'. D tempts from the past-tense framing ('photographed', 'captured'); 'crevasses' tempts plural.

SEC26B-03.note: Independent clauses joined by semicolon; a second colon (D) is not allowed after the one already in the sentence. A splice, B fused.

SEC26B-04.note: Plural 'segments'; a specific past time ('on the evening of') excludes present perfect.

SEC26B-05.note: Elliptical 'do [lengthen]' parallels 'barely lengthens'. 'were' tempts via 'nineteenth-century' but has nothing to complete; 'does/was' singular.

SEC26B-06.note: Singular 'receiver' takes 'is'; 'them' = the grains. 'domes' pulls plural.

SEC26B-07.note: 'As the crew blasted the ridge,' is the intro clause; 'loosened boulders' is the subject of 'fell'. A creates a stranded second verb; garden path attracts it.

SEC26B-08.note: Plural 'staves'; past progressive parallels 'slowly cooled'. 'wall'/'hearth' pull singular.

SEC26B-09.note: Single bunk, one hand: singular possessive 'observer's'. Plural possessive tempts from 'visitors'.

SEC26B-10.note: Semicolon-separated list (later '; and'), so the first item ends with a semicolon; copied from the parallel slot.

SEC26C-01.note: Singular 'curtain' takes 'was'; 'them' = the three painters. 'backdrops'/'flies' pull plural.

SEC26C-02.note: 'The illiterate' (adjective as noun for people) is plural; 'since' requires present perfect. 'has been' attracts readers who treat it as singular.

SEC26C-03.note: Plural 'copes'; past ('on the eve of the great fire'). Singular 'inventory'/'vestment' distract.

SEC26C-04.note: Colon after the independent clause introduces the explanation of the clue. A splice, B fused, D garbled.

SEC26C-05.note: Plural 'copyists'; interrupted action ('when floodwaters spread') takes past progressive. 'scriptorium' pulls singular.

SEC26C-06.note: Singular 'editor' takes 'was'; 'it' = the final chapter/novel being cut. 'sonnets' tempts 'were' and 'them'.

SEC26C-07.note: Singular 'toll'; past event ('at the funeral of the bell's first patron'). Present-tense framing of the opening tempts 'is'.

SEC26C-08.note: Singular 'restorer'; past progressive interrupted by 'before the councillors quit'. 'paintings' pulls plural; 'has been' tempts on aspect.

SEC26C-09.note: Only one letter book exists ('that one volume'), so the participle is supplementary and takes a comma. B is attractive and mirrors SEC26A-03, where no comma is right.

SEC26C-10.convention: generic singular definite noun ('the apprentice', parallel to 'the master printer'); 'cast' is a valid past form for either number
SEC26C-10.note: Context ('three or four boys at a time') favours plural 'apprentices', but 'In such a shop the apprentice cast new letters ... while the master printer set the pages' is fully grammatical as generic singular.

SEC26D-01.note: Singular 'diner' takes 'judges'; 'it' = the oddly precise price. 'them' tempts via 'prices' but yields a self-comparison.

SEC26D-02.note: Singular mass noun 'Bilingualism'; past ('at the height of'). Little pull beyond 'vendors' after the blank.

SEC26D-03.note: The town had one paper, so 'the Sentinel' is a nonrestrictive appositive; a dash introduces it and it runs to the sentence end (comma after 'Sentinel' belongs to the whose-clause). A attracts as a restrictive appositive.

SEC26D-04.note: Plural 'tenants'; present set by 'stays'. Parenthetical 'the interviewers found' pulls toward past 'were accepting'.

SEC26D-05.note: Singular 'study' plus 'since' gives 'has been following'. 'interns and paid classmates' pulls plural.

SEC26D-06.note: Singular 'suffix' with 'fully disappeared' needs 'has never'; 'is ... disappeared' is not standard. 'verbs' pulls plural.

SEC26D-07.note: Plural 'teams' takes 'have'; 'its' = the questionnaire's wording. 'villages' tempts 'their'.

SEC26D-08.note: Plural 'volunteers' plus 'since' gives 'have coached'. Singular 'grant'/'desk' distract.

SEC26D-09.convention: colon after an independent clause introducing an explanatory appositive at sentence end
SEC26D-09.note: Comma sets off the final appositive 'the widow of ...'. A colon is also acceptable here because the preceding clause is complete; semicolon (A) and no punctuation (C) fail.

SEC26D-10.note: 'A lone appointee' gives singular 'parliamentarian', which agrees with 'rules'. Plurals clash with 'rules'; the possessive leaves no main verb.

tells: In punctuation items, the option with a trailing comma after 'the' or a participle ('sight the,' SEC26C-04, 'newspaper the,' SEC26D-03, 'tray kept,' SEC26A-03, 'book filled,' SEC26C-09) is never the key and can be struck on sight.

Almost every verb item is a 2x2 grid (number x tense or number x pronoun) where a long modifier with a noun of the opposite number sits next to the blank; a test-taker who learns 'ignore the noun beside the blank' solves most of them. Keys are balanced across cells, so there is no letter or cell tell.
Every item with 'since' in the sentence keys the present perfect (SEC26A-04, SEC26C-02, SEC26D-05, SEC26D-06, SEC26D-08); that is the rule, but it is a single cue word repeated across five items.
SEC26B-10 is the only list item and is decided by copying the later semicolon.
near_duplicates: restrictive vs supplementary participle after a noun, mirrored keys
clause boundary after a noun followed by 'the'
appositive after a noun or name
singular or plural possessive decided by context
verb number crossed with pronoun number grid
